rows.claim: Status is one of shipped, candidate, or example first.
rows.evidence: Every table row in section 3 reads `shipped` or `not admitted` (lines 213 to 354); no row is a candidate or example first, and line 460 says the additions closed the list.
rows.fix: Status is one of *shipped* or *not admitted*. *Candidate* (listed, built when wanted) and *example first* (built as an example model, promoted only if one form proves standard) were the statuses before the 2026-11 increments, and no row carries them now.

rows.claim: A side with several ports names them in1…inN (and out1…outN where a component splits one port into N alike).
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:263 and :263 (Switch inputs in1, in2, select), :2385 and src/library.jl:2380 (PID inputs r, y, saturation, engaged, v), :309-320 (Select names the inputs after the enum), probe:73-75. Only Junction (src/library.jl:100) and Unpack (:193) use the numbered names.
rows.fix: A junction names its N inputs `in1…inN`, and `Unpack` names its outputs `out1…outN`; any other side with several ports names them by role, as `Switch` (`in1`, `in2`, `select`), the PID (`r`, `y`) and `Select` (the enum's instances) do.
rows.note: The sentence reads as a rule for every multi-port side. Low severity if it is meant only for the N-ary junction and the splitter.

rows.claim: A component with one required parameter such as Constant(value) takes it positionally. Its docstring shows the keyword form, and its tests call it.
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:346 (Constant docstring shows `Constant(value) -> Constant`); test/test_library.jl:16 and :21 call `Constant(a)` positionally; design/rules/docstring_rules.md:80-82 (the keyword form is shown only for a component with a keyword constructor).
rows.fix: Move the sentence ahead of the Constant sentence, so it reads: `The struct keeps its positional constructor. Its docstring shows the keyword form, and its tests call it. A component with one required parameter, such as Constant(value), takes it positionally.` Or, if the sentence is about Constant, write `Its docstring shows that form`.
rows.note: The antecedent of `Its` is Constant, whose docstring shows the positional form. The rule in docstring_rules.md rule 10 refers to components with keyword constructors.

rows.claim: Zero-Pole: roots real or complex; a product whose imaginary part is not zero to rounding is refused, which conjugate pairs pass, and the real coefficients then meet the existing refusals.
rows.evidence: src/library.jl:1166-1183 (coefficients_from_roots pairs each complex root with a conjugate by a tolerance 1e-12 relative to the root and refuses an unpaired root; the comment says a check on the expanded coefficients' imaginary parts misreads rounding), probe:78-85 (a conjugate pair passes, an unpaired root is refused as `not real or in conjugate pairs`, ten pairs pass).
rows.fix: Roots real or complex; a root with no conjugate partner within `1e-12` of its magnitude is refused, which conjugate pairs pass, and the real coefficients then meet the existing refusals.
rows.note: The refusal exists and the roots are exclusive with num and den; only the mechanism differs. The check on the product's imaginary part was replaced by pairing, since the product check refused exact conjugate sets of ten pairs.

rows.fix: Every row is shipped or not admitted. The first two tranches shipped first, the candidate rows of the 2026-10-30 sweep followed as increments 86 to 89, and the list is closed.

ok.claim: The discrete reset writes s0 while the flag reads true, so the state lands at the next tick and the output at the reset tick is the stale integral.
A same-tick reset would make every input a feedthrough edge, so it is not offered.
Backlash holds inside a deadband of width about itself and follows the input at half a width's offset outside it.
DiscreteLimitedIntegrator has lower, upper, s0, reset and the Int8 saturation code read off the state from stage 1; the reset is the level form with s0 clamped.
Freeze{V} over Float64 and SArray is the declared stop-gradient; a struct V is not admitted.
PID is one law q̇ = Ki ε + (ref - u_raw)/Tt, componentwise, with two independent axes hold and tracking.
DiscretePID shares ports, gate, reference rule and parameters through AbstractPID{V, Hold, Track, Fixed}.
LQRTracker has inputs x, z, z_ref as static vectors, outputs u and u_raw from stage 2, no saturation output.
DiscreteLQRTracker is over AbstractLQRTracker, forward Euler on the integrator and the correction's exact step.
The hold adds the saturation code that gates the integrator by sign and the flag engaged, with not engaged taking precedence.
v is the reference while limited or not engaged, with the own u as fallback while free.
The three axis ports sit at the output's shape and Ki sits inside the integral.
Every parameter is a V, and any of them a port by AsPort().
The weights default to b = 1 and c = 0, so the derivative acts on the measurement.
A fixed infinite Tt is refused with tracking; PID has no saturation output.
DiscretePID is forward Euler on the integral, backward Euler on the derivative filter (τd = 0 is the backward difference), and step 1 - e^{-Δt/Tt}, with Tt = 0 instant.
A second output saturated, the own clamp's Int8 code, is written to the store at the tick and published from stage 1 at the next, one tick stale.
The LQR law is u_raw = u_trim + K_fwd (z_ref - z_trim) - K_fbk (x - x_trim) + q, q̇ = ε + (ref - u_raw)/Tt, ε the gated K_int (z_ref - z).
It has the PID's two axes channel by channel, engaged per channel; the nine parameters are three gains, the trim triple, Tt, u_min, u_max, any a port by AsPort().
The tracker's Int8 code vector is the output saturated, from stage 1 off the store, one tick stale.
A tracking leaf wired from a memoryless clamp of its own output is refused as an artificial cycle.
AsPort() on the limits of RateLimiter, LimitedIntegrator and DiscreteLimitedIntegrator is not admitted.
